title: The Waiting Room (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I've been to the waiting room more times than I can say
The one at the doctor's office and the one at the end of the day
There's always a magazine from fourteen months ago
And a man who needs the chair next to you — you're the last to know

[Pre-Chorus]
I once sat in a waiting room for four and twenty minutes
For something that was meant to take ten minutes — I was in it

[Chorus]
The waiting room knows something I don't know
It knows that time is optional and patience is a show
The waiting room has magazines from years that have gone by
And everyone inside is practising the art of the goodbye
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The television in the corner has the volume set at low
It's playing something no one chose about somewhere no one'll go
A man across from me is doing something on his phone
We're all together in the waiting room — we've never been more alone

[Bridge]
Name gets called eventually — it always gets called
The doctor says "it's nothing" and you feel you've been forestalled
But in those twenty minutes something happens to your thinking
You solve a problem you'd forgotten while the overhead light's blinking

[Outro]
Waiting room knows… we're all waiting for something… waiting room knows
That's my boy
